phys_2_1 G1.issue: Lesson periods were unclear (many said '40 minutes, or 80 if...') and the unit total (480 minutes) was wrong; each lesson now has one period length and phase minutes that add up, total 760 minutes The old total '12 x 40 = 480' ignored that Lessons 4 and 12 are already 80-minute double lessons. Several other lessons cannot fit their activities in 40 minutes (for example Lesson 2 has three 8-minute stations before any discussion, Lesson 6 has two 10-minute practical stations plus calculations and lenses, Lesson 9 lists 8+20+20+5+7 = 60 minutes). I chose one period length for each lesson: double (80 min) for Lessons 2, 4, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12 and single (40 min) for Lessons 1, 3, 5, 7, 10. Total = 5 x 40 + 7 x 80 = 200 + 560 = 760 minutes, which equals 19 periods of 40 minutes, matching the 19 lessons that the KICD design suggests for this sub-strand. Teacher decision: confirm that your timetable can give double periods to these seven lessons, or say which lessons should be cut or split. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL 12 lessons: 5 single lessons x 40 minutes + 7 double lessons x 80 minutes = 200 + 560 = 760 minutes total (19 periods of 40 minutes)

Lesson 10 asks every learner to calculate 744 Hz and 661 Hz and Lesson 8 uses path-difference numbers. I kept the numbers (they are correct and help learners) but labelled them as extension or worked example, so the required learning is the explanation in words. phys_2_1 G6.issue: Lesson 10's human walk-through could not work (a walking person is far too slow to change the pitch of claps); replaced with a slowed-down scale model whose numbers are checked Amina walks at about 1 to 2 m/s while sound travels at 340 m/s, so the claps reaching Otieno and Wanjiru differ by less than 1 percent and learners cannot count any difference; the lesson claimed they would. A scale model fixes this: wave speed 1 m/s, source speed 0.5 m/s, clap every 1 s. Gap between wavefronts ahead = (1 - 0.5) x 1 = 0.5 m, so a wavefront arrives every 0.5 s (2 per second); behind = (1 + 0.5) x 1 = 1.5 m, so one every 1.5 s (0.67 per second). I checked it against f' = f v/(v - u) = 1 x 1/0.5 = 2 Hz and f v/(v + u) = 1/1.5 = 0.67 Hz. Teacher decision: this changes the activity design; confirm that chalk and string (or a compass on paper) are available and that you prefer this to the original walk. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL First, a scale model of the moving source in an open space. A walking learner is far too slow to change the pitch of a real clap, so the wave is slowed down: 1 m on the ground stands for 1 second of wave travel. One learner (Amina) acts as the siren and walks steadily along a chalk line at 0.5 m/s while a timekeeper claps once per second; a partner marks Amina's position at each clap. Second, groups draw the wavefronts on the ground (string and chalk) or on paper (compass): from each mark a circle whose radius is 1 m for every second since that clap, so the circles start from successive positions of the source. The circles are bunched up in front of Amina (0.5 m apart) and stretched behind …
